issue.title: Different order in files passed from the command line produces different (and incorrect) output

labels.name: High effort 🏋
labels.description: Difficult solution or problem to solve

labels.name: Duplicate 🐫
labels.description: Duplicate of an already existing issue

repository.name: pylint
repository.description: It's not just a linter that annoys you!

issue.body:
### Steps to reproduce

I prepared a minimal repro here:
https://github.com/andreaTP/pylint_order_bug

### Current behavior

Cloning the example project and running:
```bash
python3 -m pylint test2/test3/test.py test2/test4/test.py test/__init__.py
```
R0801 (similarity) is reported on an incorrect file:
```
test/__init__.py:1:0: R0801: Similar lines in 2 files
```

### Expected behavior

Cloning the example project and running:
```bash
python3 -m pylint test2/test3/test.py test2/test4/test.py test/__init__.py
```
 produces the same result as:
```bash
python3 -m pylint test/__init__.py test2/test3/test.py test2/test4/test.py
```
Such as `R0801` is reported on the correct file:
```
test2/test4/test.py:1:0: R0801: Similar lines in 2 files
```

### pylint --version output
```
pylint 2.5.2
astroid 2.4.1
Python 3.6.9 (default, Apr 18 2020, 01:56:04) 
[GCC 8.4.0]
```

issue.title: pylint is confusing ExitStack() and AsyncExitStack() when both are used

labels.name: Needs PR
labels.description: This issue is accepted, sufficiently specified and now needs an implementation

repository.name: pylint
repository.description: It's not just a linter that annoys you!

issue.body:
### Bug description

pylint is confusing ExitStack() and AsyncExitStack() when analyzing two different modules using each.

Consider as a minimized example, the following two modules.

sync.py
```
from contextlib import ExitStack
def sync_stack_use():
    stack = ExitStack()
    stack.pop_all().close()
```

async.py
```
from contextlib import AsyncExitStack
def async_stack_use():
    stack = AsyncExitStack()
    stack.pop_all().aclose()
```


### Configuration

_No response_

### Command used

```shell
1. pylint --disable=all --enable=no-member sync.py
2. pylint --disable=all --enable=no-member async.py
3. pylint --disable=all --enable=no-member sync.py async.py
4. pylint --disable=all --enable=no-member async.py sync.py
```


### Pylint output

```shell
1. no finding
2. no finding
3. async.py:4:4: E1101: Instance of 'ExitStack' has no 'aclose' member; maybe 'close'? (no-member)
4. sync.py:4:4: E1101: Instance of 'AsyncExitStack' has no 'close' member; maybe 'aclose'? (no-member)
```


### Expected behavior

1. no finding
2. no finding
3. no finding
4. no finding

### Pylint version

```shell
pylint 2.15.2
astroid 2.12.9
Python 3.8.5 (tags/v3.8.5:580fbb0, Jul 20 2020, 15:57:54) [MSC v.1924 64 bit (AMD64)]
```


### OS / Environment

Windows (reproduced also on Ubuntu 20.04 LTS).

### Additional dependencies

_No response_

issue.title: Pylint does not report "unused-import" if there are quotes around type hint

repository.name: pylint
repository.description: It's not just a linter that annoys you!

issue.body:
### Bug description

I used [`hatch`](https://hatch.pypa.io) to create this example repo (`pipx install hatch`).

* clone the example repo: https://github.com/hofrob/pylint-unused-import-quotes
* execute `hatch run pylint -d all -e W0611 test_pylint/ tests/`
* pylint should report an unused import in `test_pylint/baz.py`
* remove quotes from type hint in `test_pylint.foo.foo_baz` function (around `bar.SomeClass`)
* execute `hatch run pylint -d all -e W0611 test_pylint/ tests/`
* pylint correctly reports an unused import

Those two things should be unrelated I'd say. No idea why quotes (even if they don't make sense) influence an unused import warning in a completely unrelated file.

### Configuration

_No response_

### Command used

```shell
pylint -d all -e W0611 test_pylint/ tests/
```


### Pylint output

```shell
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Your code has been rated at 10.00/10 (previous run: 10.00/10, +0.00)
```

### Expected behavior

```
************* Module test_pylint.baz
test_pylint/baz.py:1:0: W0611: Unused bar imported from test_pylint (unused-import)

------------------------------------------------------------------

```

### Pylint version

```shell

astroid 2.12.10
```
